content: Advise these patients to use effective contraception during treatment and for five months following the final dose. If vomiting or diarrhea occurs during therapy, it may interfere with the absorption of oral contraceptives, potentially reducing their effectiveness. In such cases, recommend the use of an additional non-oral method of effective contraception. There is no available data on the presence of miltefosine in human or animal breast milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its impact on milk production. Due to the potential for serious adverse reactions, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment and for five months after the last dose. Administer the medication with meals to minimize gastrointestinal side effects. Capsules should be swallowed whole and not chewed or broken apart. Patients should be instructed to complete the full course of therapy as prescribed. For formulary information, create a list of plans to compare the drug's formulary status with other medications in the same class. This list can be saved and edited as needed. Note that formulary information may vary between plans and is subject to change. Contact the relevant plan provider for the most up-to-date information. The above information is provided for general educational purposes.
